answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The ripple of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Every claim climbs the summit of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the dawn re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on invitation quota tree, taxed when attestations come from one subnet.
